correctness.rationale: The scalar sine secant inequality is strict for unequal arguments. Applied to the lifted vertex map, it proves injectivity through the closed spectral threshold, and equivariance plus compactness yields an endpoint homeomorphism. At equality, the displayed even or odd edge configuration gives a singular differential. For every larger coupling, explicit closure-respecting cosine assignments produce exactly one negative eigenvalue: even cycles have a simple top Fourier eigenmode; for odd cycles the positive rank-one correction has one-dimensional kernel on the double top eigenspace. The map has degree +1, so a regular negative-orientation inverse branch forces at least two positive-orientation branches. Sard and local inversion yield an open set. The code checks 228 sample negative-orientation constructions; no finite test substitutes for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 ring work proves a sufficient open diffeomorphism range and studies the Lyapunov range, but does not classify the closed homeomorphism boundary and all stronger coupling strengths. The earlier general-network paper makes its sharpness assertion for sinusoidal trees; that assertion cannot be substituted for a full global ring inverse-count theorem. A previously established local three-branch result only treats coupling sufficiently near the first threshold; it does not imply persistence at arbitrary higher coupling. The new rank-one orientation construction and degree argument supply that missing global implication. Targeted primary-literature and prior-claim comparisons found no stronger covering statement. value.rationale: The question whether a discrete phase map can recover global invertibility at stronger coupling is a natural unresolved global parameter question left by the sufficient spectral and Lyapunov results. The result gives a complete answer for all ring sizes and all positive coupling strengths, including the singular yet globally bijective endpoint and a robust three-preimage obstruction on the entire supercritical half-line. The parity-dependent construction reveals a nontrivial rank-one spectral mechanism absent from a local fold calculation; this is more than a routine constant improvement or a finite-instance check.
